name: Ahikam
overview: Ahikam was a male figure known primarily as the son of Shaphan, as recorded in 2 Kings 22:12. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His identity is grounded chiefly in his paternal connection to Shaphan.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahikam means '[my] brother stands,' reflecting a Hebrew origin. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may suggest loyalty or support within familial or communal relationships.
familyAndRelationships: Ahikam is explicitly identified as the son of Shaphan in Scripture (2 Kings 22:12). Additionally, it is inferred that he was the father of Gedaliah, as suggested in 2 Kings 25:22. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Ahikam holds significance in the biblical narrative primarily through his lineage and his role connected to key figures in Judah's history. As the son of Shaphan, a notable scribe, Ahikam's family was involved in important events during the reign of King Josiah. His inferred fatherhood of Gedaliah links him to the governance of Judah following the Babylonian conquest, highlighting his family's ongoing influence in biblical history.
